notes.summary: Primary-source foundations checked for bounded Hermitian comparison, local product calculus, bounded exponential existence, scalar uniqueness, and full-mass Kähler uniqueness. None establishes the named factor's mass collapse.
notes.detailedSummary: The source applications are restricted to bounded approximations, local bounded products, and full-mass potentials on the Kähler base. Unbounded greatestness and joint varying-data convergence are reconstructed below, rather than attributed to an Lp theorem. No private proof, candidate article, earlier report, or author factor construction was used.
notes.text:
The following primary texts were opened and their relevant statements inspected independently.

Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math. 149 (1982), author-hosted PDF https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf: Theorem 2.1 gives decreasing convergence of mixed locally bounded psh products when the limit remains locally bounded; Corollary 2.2 supplies multilinearity. Theorems 6.9–6.10 give zero outer capacity of pluripolar sets and decay of local sublevel capacities. Applications below concern bounded truncations, annuli where the limiting potential is bounded, and neighborhoods of the single base pole.

Kołodziej–Nguyen, Weak solutions to the complex Monge–Ampère equation on Hermitian manifolds, arXiv:1312.5491v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491: Theorem 0.2 applies to bounded ω-psh functions on a compact Hermitian manifold. Writing mε=inf(φ−(1−ε)ψ), its comparison integral over {φ<(1−ε)ψ+mε+s} has factor 1+Cs/ε^n for 0<s<ε^3/(16B). A smooth positive metric on a compact manifold satisfies the required torsion bounds defining B. This is used below with a strict exponential gap. It requires no positive lower-mass assumption.

Nguyen, The complex Monge–Ampère type equation on compact Hermitian manifolds and Applications, arXiv:1501.00891v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891: Theorem 0.1 gives the continuous bounded positive-exponent solution for nonzero nonnegative Lp data, p>1. Lemma 2.3 orders bounded solutions by their densities. Corollary 2.7 gives uniqueness of the scalar in the continuous zero-exponent equation. These results are applied only to bounded positive densities. This source uses dd^c twice the task's operator; its potential is therefore u/2 and its exponent is 2λ.

Dinew, Uniqueness and stability in E(X,ω), arXiv:0804.3407v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.3407: Theorem 1.2 gives uniqueness up to constants for equal Monge–Ampère measures of full-mass potentials on a compact Kähler manifold. Its application below is exclusively to (P^k,κ), with mass one. No nonclosed uniqueness conclusion follows from it.

Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2: Bounds on Monge–Ampère volumes, Algebraic Geometry 9 (2022), primary journal PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf: Section 1.1.1 constructs bounded smooth-background correction products using local closed dominating forms. Lemma 1.2 supplies maximum locality and the contact-set product inequality. Only this local bounded Bedford–Taylor calculus is used; the paper's envelope and volume theorems are not invoked.

All potentials below belong to the canonical subclass stipulated in the task. Continuous approximations and genuine decreasing psh limits preserve this convention. No almost-everywhere alteration of a potential occurs. The supplied definition of the non-pluripolar extended product is used through its bounded truncations, with the smooth-background correction terms retained.

The source audit is saved in source_audit.md. The shell has no network access; primary PDFs were inspected through the available web tool. No supervised compute service was supplied or discovered. Only small local diagnostics were run; no resource-heavy computation was undertaken. These are ordinary proof drafts, and source access or successful execution does not certify their correctness.

notes.summary: Explicit radial proof of the genuine base probability, absence of a pole atom, positivity, L1 but no Lp integrability, the exact first-moment threshold, and direct all-scale stretching witnesses.
notes.detailedSummary: For s=log|z|², r=e^s/(1+e^s), x=1−log r, and A=αx^(α−1), the radial cumulative Monge–Ampère mass is T^k, where T=A+(1−A)r. Its endpoints are 0 and 1. The density is positive smooth off o, including infinity, and decreases radially. The moment is finite exactly when α<k/(k+1). Explicit witnesses establish E_env by its defining inequalities, without using envelope equality or asserting bounded ordinary type.
notes.text:
Work on Y=P^k with ∫κ^k=1 and the task's dd^c. In the affine chart z0=1 put R=|z|², s=log R, ρ(s)=log(1+e^s), r=ρ'=e^s/(1+e^s), and x=1−log r. Thus ψ=log r, x ranges from infinity at o to 1 at the hyperplane at infinity, and x'=−(1−r). Write A=αx^(α−1). For F=ρ+uα one obtains

F'=T=A+(1−A)r,
T'=r(1−r)(1−A)+α(1−α)x^(α−2)(1−r)².

Both terms in T' are nonnegative, and T'>0 at every finite s. The radial determinant formula, obtained by differentiating a smooth radial potential, gives the annular mass element kT^(k−1)T' ds. For κ^k the corresponding element is kr^(k−1)r' ds. Consequently

qα=T^(k−1)T'/(r^(k−1)r').

This identity holds for actual smooth measures on Y\{o}; uα is smooth there, including across the hyperplane at infinity.

The potential is genuinely κ-psh. Indeed χ(t)=1−(1−t)^α is increasing and convex on t≤0, with 0≤χ'≤α<1. Locally, if κ=dd^cρ, the function χ(p−ρ)+ρ is a convex increasing function of the two psh inputs p=ψ+ρ and ρ: its partial derivatives are χ' and 1−χ', and its Hessian is χ'' times the positive matrix [[1,−1],[−1,1]]. This proves the required local psh property, including the canonical value −∞ at o. It also excludes an arbitrary representative change.

As s→−∞, T∼αx^(α−1)→0; as s→∞, T→1. Integrating the annular mass formula therefore gives actual mass one off o. The non-pluripolar construction assigns zero mass to o. Thus the extended product is precisely qακ^k, a probability with no pole atom; there is no missing boundary or infinity contribution.

For explicit positivity and monotonicity, write

qα=D^(k−1)B,
D=1+A e^(−s),
B=1−A+α(1−α)x^(α−2)e^(−s).

Here B>0. Moreover A'=α(1−α)x^(α−2)(1−r), so D'<0. The derivative of the last term of B is that term times [(2−α)(1−r)/x−1], while the derivative of 1−A is −A'<0. The inequality (1−r)/x<1/2 follows from x−2+2e^(1−x)>0 for x≥1; its minimum is log 2. Hence B'<0 and qα decreases with s. At infinity qα=1−α. In particular qα≥1−α>0 everywhere off the pole.

Near the pole,

qα∼α^k(1−α)e^{k(x−1)}x^{k(α−1)−1}.

The base volume has x-density ke^{k(1−x)}. The probability calculation already proves L1 integrability. For every p>1, qα^pκ^k has an exponentially growing tail proportional to e^{k(p−1)x} times a power of x, so its integral diverges. Thus this is genuine L1 data outside every Lp, p>1.

The tail probability of x is Tα(x)^k, where Tα(x)=αx^(α−1)+(1−αx^(α−1))e^(1−x). Layer-cake integration gives

−Mα=∫(x^α−1)qακ^k=α∫_1^∞ x^(α−1)Tα(x)^k dx.

Its integrand is asymptotic to α^(k+1)x^{(k+1)(α−1)}. The integral is finite exactly for α<k/(k+1). It is strictly positive when finite, hence Mα is a finite negative number. At equality the divergence is logarithmic; above equality it is a power divergence. This proves the stated explicit constant, including its endpoints of applicability.

The all-scale class is verified directly. For each real t≥1 choose L≥1 so that tαL^(α−1)≤1, and set a_t=t[1−(L−ψ)^α], with canonical value −∞ at o. The same convex-composition argument makes a_t κ-psh, because its derivative lies in [0,1]. Since L≥1, a_t≤t uα pointwise, including at the common pole. Thus t^−1a_t≤uα. Together with uα≤0 this proves uα∈E_env(Y,κ,0). Pullback gives exactly the defining witnesses on any Hermitian product (X0×Y,h0+κ). It does not prove or assert uα~0 in ordinary bounded type; that assertion would fail because uα has a pole.

Artifacts: inputs.json and checks.py contain the radial formulas and diagnostic inputs. Rerun with python checks.py > checks_output.json. Across 21 parameter pairs, quadrature plus the exact tail yielded mass residual at most 3.34×10^−15, and all sampled logarithmic density increments with increasing x were positive. These finite observations are checks only; the preceding derivations are the mathematical arguments.

notes.summary: Actual truncation threshold and greatest separated exponential family reconstructed on every Hermitian product. Under the assumed zero-lower-mass factor hypothesis, the product also has zero lower mass.
notes.detailedSummary: For any compact Hermitian factor, bounded base truncation equations give b_H(f)=binomial(m+k,m)V0. Smooth saturation approximations construct the base unbounded exponential solution. A bounded maximum and modified Hermitian comparison show that every genuine full-product exponential subsolution lies below every separated approximation, proving greatestness after passage to the limit. All limiting products have mass b and no pole-fiber mass. This result does not depend on proving F.
notes.text:
Let X0 be any compact connected Hermitian m-fold, V0=∫h0^m, X=X0×Y, H=h0+κ, dV=(h0^m/V0)⊗κ^k, and b=binomial(m+k,m)V0. For a genuine base potential z, bounded truncations and multilinearity give the actual identity

MA_ext,H(z∘prY)=binomial(m+k,m)h0^m⊗MA_ext,κ(z).

Indeed the bounded formula follows by dimension from the smooth-background correction expansion. Restricting it to {z>−L} and increasing L proves the extended formula. In particular it retains all correction terms and assigns no mass to the pole fiber whenever the base product assigns none to o.

For the original density truncations qℓ=min(qα,ℓ), put Qℓ=∫qℓκ^k. These densities extend continuously and positively across o by the constant value ℓ. Define Zℓ(s)^k=Qℓ^−1∫_{−∞}^s qℓ(t)d(r(t)^k). The function with derivative Zℓ−r and value zero at infinity is a bounded genuine κ-psh potential: Zℓ is increasing, and the derivative is integrable at both ends. The normalized density qℓ/Qℓ decreases radially, so its cumulative distribution dominates r^k; hence Zℓ≥r and the potential has supremum zero. Its actual Monge–Ampère measure is Qℓ^−1qℓκ^k. Pullback solves the continuous product equation with scalar b/Qℓ. The verified continuous Hermitian scalar uniqueness identifies this with the original c_H(min(f,ℓ)). Since Qℓ↑1,

b_H(f)=limℓ b/Qℓ=b.

The pullback of uα therefore solves the finite-mass threshold equation MA_ext,H(uα∘prY)=b f dV, has supremum zero, and belongs to the defining all-scale class by n2.

Here is the comparison extension needed for greatestness. Let W be a bounded continuous solution for a bounded density g bounded below by a positive constant, and let s be any genuine exponential subsolution for the same g. Then t=max(s,W) is bounded: W supplies its lower bound and global quasi-psh boundedness above supplies its upper bound. The local maximum and contact inequalities give MA_H(t)≥e^{λt}g dV. To justify this using only bounded calculus, first truncate s below a constant smaller than inf W. On {s>W} locality identifies the product with the extended product of s; on {s≤W} the contact inequality bounds it below by the product of W. No product is assigned to an almost-everywhere replacement.

Suppose M=sup(t−W)>0. For small ε, set mε=inf(W−(1−ε)t) and Aε,s={W<(1−ε)t+mε+s}. On this set, t−W≥M−2ε||t||∞−s. Thus, after choosing ε sufficiently small,

MA_H((1−ε)t)≥(1−ε)^N e^{λM/2}MA_H(W)

there, with a factor strictly greater than one. The modified comparison theorem bounds the same integral by (1+Cs/ε^N)∫_{Aε,s}MA_H(W). This integral is positive: a nonempty strict near-maximum set of a canonical quasi-psh function relative to a continuous function has positive volume, by its local submean property, and g is bounded below. Sending s to zero is contradictory. Therefore s≤W. This proof applies to subsolutions, including unbounded ones; bounded uniqueness alone would not suffice.

Construct the base exponential solution as follows. Choose a smooth nondecreasing concave function S on [0,∞), equal to its argument up to 1 and constant after 2, and define gℓ=ℓS(qα/ℓ), ℓ≥1. Then gℓ is smooth positive on Y, constant near o, nonincreasing with s, increasing with ℓ, and tends to qα. It satisfies 1−α≤gℓ≤qα. The bounded existence theorem supplies wℓ with MAκ(wℓ)=e^{λwℓ}gℓκ^k. Bounded comparison makes wℓ decrease with ℓ. Since uα≤0 and MAκ(uα)=qακ^k≥e^{λuα}gℓκ^k, the comparison extension just proved gives wℓ≥uα. Comparison with the constant solution for density 1−α also gives wℓ≤λ^−1log(1/(1−α)).

Uniqueness makes wℓ invariant under the unitary group acting on z′, so it is radial. Continuous radial solutions are smooth here without invoking unbounded regularity. On an annulus, the radial bounded-product formula gives Tℓ=ρ'+wℓ' and

(Tℓ^k)'=e^{λwℓ}gℓ(r^k)'.

The right side is continuous and positive; convexity first gives a continuous positive Tℓ, and this equation then bootstraps to smoothness. Near R=0, Tℓ/R is the positive kth root of an integral over [0,1] of smooth coefficients involving wℓ(Rz); the equation wℓ,R=Tℓ/R−1/(1+R) bootstraps through R=0. The equivalent integral from infinity gives the same extension there.

One also has wℓ'≥0. Otherwise d=wℓ' has a negative interior minimum, since d tends to zero at both ends. At that minimum Tℓ<r, Tℓ'=r', and Tℓ''≥r''. Differentiating the logarithmic equation yields

(log gℓ)'=(k−1)r'(1/Tℓ−1/r)+(Tℓ''−r'')/r'−λd>0,

contradicting the nonincreasing density.

The genuine decreasing limit w exists, is locally bounded away from o, and satisfies the equation there by bounded local convergence. It is radial nondecreasing. At infinity it is continuous: convexity bounds T≤1, hence 0≤w'≤1−r, an integrable bound; a higher value on the infinity divisor would contradict the canonical submean property. The integral equation there bootstraps to smoothness. Explicitly, with δ=1−r, 1−T^k is an integral from 0 to δ of a smooth coefficient involving w. Dividing by δ and using w_δ=−[T−(1−δ)]/[δ(1−δ)] first extends the derivative continuously, then extends every derivative.

Each bounded equation has ∫e^{λwℓ}gℓκ^k=1. Dominated convergence, using e^{λwℓ}≤1/(1−α) and gℓ≤qα, gives ∫e^{λw}qακ^k=1. The actual extended base product therefore has full mass one. Its pole is genuine: if w had a finite lower limit there, then T^k(s)≥C Tα^k(s), C>0, forcing w'≥C^{1/k}Tα−r near −∞. The integral of Tα∼α(1−s)^(α−1) diverges, contradicting a finite lower limit. Hence w(o)=−∞. The equation is smooth away from o, and both sides give zero mass to o. The density weighting means the measure e^{λw}(qακ^k), with e^{λw(o)}=0; it does not require interpreting a pointwise expression 0 times an infinite density.

Set Uℓ=(log b)/λ+wℓ∘prY. The product identity makes this the bounded solution for gℓ∘prY. Every full-product exponential subsolution for f=qα∘prY is also a subsolution for gℓ∘prY, and the comparison extension gives s≤Uℓ. Passing to the limit shows s≤U=(log b)/λ+w∘prY. This U itself solves the required equation and has finite mass b. It is therefore the greatest original solution, not merely one separated solution. This proves B.

Finally, if v_−(h0)=0 is assumed, bounded factor potentials pulled back to X give masses binomial(m+k,m) times their factor masses, so v_−(H)=0. Such an h0 cannot be closed: a closed Hermitian background has bounded-potential mass V0 by Stokes. Thus this proves the zero-lower-mass and nonclosed portions of A conditionally on its factor hypothesis. It does not establish that hypothesis for the named factor.

notes.summary: Complete radial selection, exact centering dichotomy, and joint varying-alpha/varying-exponent stability with no rate constraint; intrinsic critical-subsolution characterization remains confined to the separated sector.
notes.detailedSummary: Monotone exponential weighting gives r≤T_lambda,alpha≤T_alpha and hence u_alpha≤v_lambda,alpha≤0. These bounds prove normalized convergence in base L1, capacity, and locally uniformly including infinity. For alpha_j→alpha and lambda_j→0, densities converge in L1 and the same argument applies jointly. Uniform moment tails below the critical exponent give the finite scalar error limit; compact-set integration gives divergence at and above it, even for approach from below. Kähler full-mass uniqueness provides the order characterization, without asserting nonclosed global uniqueness.
notes.text:
Use the actual base solution w=w_{λ,α} from n3, a=sup w=w at infinity, and v=w−a. Let T=ρ'+w'. The actual radial probability equation says

T(s)^k=∫_{−∞}^s e^{λw(t)}d(Tα(t)^k).

Because w is nondecreasing and the total weighted mass is one, the increasing weight e^{λw} moves cumulative mass to the right: for every s, the weighted cumulative probability is at most the original cumulative probability Tα(s)^k. One elementary proof compares the weight with its value at s on both sides of s and uses its total mean one. Together with w'≥0 this gives

r≤T≤Tα.

Integration from infinity now gives the decisive bounds

v(s)=−∫_s^∞(T−r)dt,
uα(s)=−∫_s^∞(Tα−r)dt,
uα≤v≤0.

These bounds concern the supremum-normalized potential; they do not omit or absorb a scalar error. In particular the all-scale witnesses for uα also witness v∈E_env(Y,κ,0) and its product counterpart.

Put I_{λ,α}=∫e^{λv}qακ^k. Mass one gives e^{λa}=1/I_{λ,α}, so a≥0 and λa=−log I_{λ,α}. For fixed α, the bounds on v imply I_{λ,α}→1. Thus the exact original product scalar is cλ=b e^{λa}→b.

The stronger joint statement follows directly. Let αj→α∈(0,1), λj→0, with no relation between the rates. The formulas of n2 give qαj→qα pointwise off o, and every density has mass one. Since min(qαj,qα)→qα and is dominated by qα, integration gives ||qαj−qα||L1→0.

Write uj=uαj, vj=v_{λj,αj}, aj=a_{λj,αj}, and Ij=∫e^{λjvj}qαjκ^k. Because uj≤vj≤0,

0≤1−Ij≤∫(1−e^{λjuj})qαjκ^k.

Replace qαj in this upper bound by qα with an error at most its L1 distance. At every point off o, uj remains finite and converges to uα, so dominated convergence against the fixed probability qακ^k makes the remaining integral tend to zero. Consequently Ij→1, λjaj→0, and c_j/b=1/Ij→1.

The actual exponential densities also converge in L1 to qα: their difference from qαj is bounded in L1 by 2(1−Ij)/Ij. Their radial cumulative probabilities Tj^k therefore converge uniformly to Tα^k. Taking kth roots gives pointwise convergence Tj→Tα. On every interval [s0,∞), the bound 0≤Tj−r≤Tαj−r=αj x^(αj−1)(1−r) supplies a common integrable bound, with exponential decay at infinity. Hence

sup_{s≥s0}|vj(s)−uα(s)|≤∫_{s0}^∞|Tj−Tα|dt→0.

This proves local uniform convergence on Y\{o}, including the infinity hyperplane. Choose α+<1 containing all sufficiently late αj. The common bound |vj|≤x^{α+}−1 is integrable against κ^k, since its x-volume tail decays exponentially. Dominated convergence proves base L1 convergence.

For each ε>0, local uniform convergence puts the set {|vj−uα|>ε} inside an arbitrarily small pole ball for sufficiently large j. The pole is pluripolar. The verified local capacity theorem makes these balls have arbitrarily small capacity. On a fixed coordinate ball, κ=dd^cρ; adding ρ to test functions 0≤φ≤1 and scaling their uniformly bounded range bounds the global κ-capacity by a constant times local Bedford–Taylor capacity. Thus vj→uα in base Kähler capacity. The common pole itself has capacity zero; no potential value is changed there.

Pullback preserves L1 convergence by Fubini with the stipulated product probability volume, and preserves local uniform convergence off X0×{o}. No product-capacity statement is used or claimed. Fixed α is the special case αj=α, so this proves the entire-family assertions C as well as the normalized assertions of G.

For centering, set

Dj=(1−Ij)/λj=∫[(1−e^{λjvj})/λj]qαjκ^k.

The integrand lies between 0 and −vj≤−uαj, and on every compact subset away from o it converges uniformly to −uα. If α<k/(k+1), choose α+<k/(k+1) above all late αj. The exact tail formula of n2 gives, uniformly in those αj,

∫_{x>L}(x^{αj}−1)qαjκ^k
=(L^{αj}−1)Tαj(L)^k+αj∫_L^∞x^(αj−1)Tαj(x)^k dx
≤C L^{(k+1)α+−k}→0.

This uniform tail control and the compact convergence imply Dj→−Mα. Since aj=−log Ij/λj and −log Ij/(1−Ij)→1, aj→−Mα. Therefore wj=vj+aj→uα−Mα in L1 and locally uniformly off the pole. The same holds for product scalar-centering, since Uj−(log b)/λj=wj∘prY. For fixed α this proves D's error limit λ^−1log(cλ/b)=aλ→−Mα.

If α≥k/(k+1), n2 gives ∫(−uα)qακ^k=∞. On each compact complement of a pole ball the integral defining Dj converges to the corresponding integral of −uα. Exhaustion therefore gives Dj→∞, whether αj approaches from above or below. Hence aj≥Dj→∞. Nevertheless λjaj=−log Ij→0. Since vj→uα locally uniformly off o, wj=vj+aj tends to +∞ locally uniformly there. This proves E and G's divergent-centering assertions without any rate condition. A finite moment for every individual αj below the critical value is no obstacle to this exhaustion argument.

The selection has an intrinsic characterization. For every genuine κ-psh z, its non-pluripolar mass is at most one: each bounded canonical truncation has mass one by Stokes, and the restricted products defining the non-pluripolar measure have mass at most one. Therefore MA_ext,κ(z)≥qακ^k forces mass one and equality. The verified full-mass Kähler uniqueness theorem gives z=uα+C, with equality of the canonical representatives, including the pole. Consequently uα is the unique supremum-zero critical subsolution in the separated sector. When Mα is finite, the condition ∫z qακ^k≤0 is precisely C≤−Mα, so uα−Mα is the greatest such critical subsolution. This is an order characterization for the actual L1 measure, not scalar uniqueness alone. In the infinite-moment regime every finite constant shift has integral −∞, so that integral constraint has no greatest finite element; supremum normalization still selects uα uniquely.

The limiting reference is the fixed ordinary model 0, and the retained class is exactly E_env with the explicit all-scale witnesses from n2. No moving singular model, bounded ordinary type, arbitrary-density stability, global nonclosed potential uniqueness, or original-programme completion is inferred.

notes.summary: Named factor geometry, genuine nonclosed metric, and V0=24π verified; v_−(h0)=0 remains unproved. Its exact missing step is vertical-energy saturation, and t-only potentials cannot provide it.
notes.detailedSummary: The quotient is a compact connected complex threefold with elliptic fibers over P1×P1. Direct calculations give dd^c h0=2α0β0, dd^c(h0²)=0, fiber volume 4π, and ∫(h0+dd^c u)³=24π−6E_vertical(u). Thus mass collapse is equivalent to supremal bounded-potential vertical energy 4π. A uniform positive lower bound holds in the t-only sector. This does not disprove unrestricted collapse, but leaves F and the named zero-lower-mass example uncertified.
notes.text:
Consider the exact quotient in F. The map [z:w]↦([z],[w]) makes its cover a holomorphic C* bundle over P1×P1: locally choose nonzero holomorphic representatives for z and w, and their relative coefficient is a coordinate ξ∈C*. The deck map sends ξ to e^{2π}ξ. It acts freely and properly discontinuously, as t=log(||w||²/||z||²) increases by 4π. The quotient is locally a holomorphic bundle with fiber E=C*/e^{2πZ}, equivalently C/(2πZ+2πiZ) in log ξ. This fiber is compact. A locally trivial compact-fiber bundle over the compact connected base is compact and connected. Its complex dimension is 2+1=3.

The pullback mass-one Fubini–Study forms satisfy α0²=β0²=0 and ∫_{P1×P1}α0β0=1. In the specified normalization,

dd^c t=K:=β0−α0.

Although t is not a global real function on the quotient, dt and d^c t descend because deck translation adds a constant. Put v=dt∧d^c t. It is a nonnegative (1,1) form, strictly positive on the vertical complex line. The form h0=α0+β0+v is therefore smooth and strictly positive: a vector annihilated by the horizontal summands is vertical, where v is positive. It descends exactly as asserted.

Direct differentiation gives dh0=−dt∧K, which is nonzero, so this metric is genuinely nonclosed. Also dd^c v=−K²=2α0β0 and hence dd^c h0=2α0β0. Since h0²=(α0+β0)²+2(α0+β0)v and the horizontal forms are closed, dd^c(h0²)=4(α0+β0)α0β0=0.

On a fiber, t=log|ξ|² plus a base constant and d^c t=(1/(2π))d arg ξ. The periods are 4π for t and 2π for arg ξ. Thus ∫_E v=4π. The wedge expansion h0³=6α0β0v now gives V0=24π. For k=2, binomial(5,3)V0=240π. The base moment threshold is 2/3 by n2; these numerical constants are proved independently of mass collapse.

For a smooth genuine h0-psh u, expansion and Stokes yield

∫(h0+dd^c u)³=∫h0³+3∫h0(dd^c u)²,

because dd^c(h0²)=0 and ∫(dd^c u)³=0. Moreover

∫h0(dd^c u)²=∫u dd^c u∧dd^c h0=−2∫du∧d^c u∧α0∧β0.

Therefore

∫MA_h0(u)=24π−6E_vertical(u),
E_vertical(u):=∫du∧d^c u∧α0∧β0.

For bounded genuine quasi-psh u the same identity follows from the ordinary local bounded-product calculus, defining u dd^c u by its Bedford–Taylor products and integrating by parts against the closed form α0β0. Equivalently the local Sobolev gradient of a bounded quasi-psh function defines this finite energy. The global correction expansion and Stokes remove the other terms exactly as above. Consequently the missing collapse claim is precisely

sup{E_vertical(u): u bounded genuine h0-psh}=4π.

No sequence attaining this supremum has been constructed here.

A restricted failed approach can be ruled out. For smooth periodic u=u(t), set p=u'. Positivity is exactly |p|≤1 and p'≥−1. Direct integration gives mass 6∫_0^{4π}(1−p²)dt, because the term (1−p²)p' integrates to zero. The mean of p is zero. If max p<1/2 or min p>−1/2, the inequality p²≤(max p+min p)p−(max p)(min p) gives ∫(1−p²)dt≥2π.
